did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jerusalem is described in this chapter as a rebellious and defiled city that does not listen to the Lord or accept correction.
Did you know? Zephaniah uses images of roaring lions and evening wolves to describe the corrupt officials and judges in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Despite the city’s sins, the righteous Lord is in her midst and brings his justice to light every morning.
Did you know? The Lord hoped that Jerusalem would learn to fear him and accept correction, but she continued to rise early and corrupt her ways.
Did you know? The vision of redemption includes a change among the nations as well: the Lord will give them “pure speech,” and they will call on his name and serve him together.
Did you know? After pride and sin are removed, the Lord promises to leave in Jerusalem a humble and lowly people who will take refuge in his name.
Did you know? The remnant of Israel is described as a people who do no wrong, speak no lies, and use no deceitful tongue; therefore, they will be able to live in safety without fear.
Did you know? The Lord is described as a mighty warrior who saves his people, rejoices over them in love, and delights in them with singing.
Did you know? The Lord promises to save the lame and gather the outcast, and to turn their shame into praise and renown.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the Lord promises to gather the exiles and restore their fortunes in the sight of all the nations.
